claims.statement: A component evaluation pairs each heatmap with independently tuned MCTS and introduces an empirical nearest-neighbor-rank control.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Sections 3 and 5, Equations 5-7

claims.statement: GT-Prior uses rank frequencies from solved instances; no neural weights or temperature are learned, but MCTS parameters are selected offline.

evidence.locator: Section 5.1 Equations 5-7; Appendix C; Appendix L raw vectors

claims.statement: Six search settings are explored using separate uniform tuning data; SHAP describes within-space associations.

evidence.locator: Sections 3.3-3.5 and 4.1; Table 12; Appendix I

claims.statement: Table 1 GT-Prior gaps are 0.50%, 0.85%, 2.14%; other methods are better at smaller scales; MCTS times are per-instance equivalent sequential times.

evidence.locator: Computational environment; Table 1 caption and rows

claims.statement: GT-Prior has strong synthetic transfer but the medium TSPLIB uniform-tuned gap is 10.08%, compared with 0.55% after instance-level selection.

evidence.locator: Tables 2-3 and 8-11; Appendix G protocol

claims.statement: Dagger heatmaps come through Xia et al.; original conventional results/timings may be borrowed; Fast-T2T-MCTS adaptation is reproduced here.

evidence.locator: Tables 1/6 captions; Appendix B Fast-T2T note

claims.statement: Euclidean TSP-specific actions, empirical and expensive tuning, and other search mechanisms limit the conclusions.

evidence.locator: Appendix M complete limitations

claims.statement: This is an empirical study of neural heatmaps and non-neural search, not a learned neural-solver architecture.

evidence.locator: Introduction/evaluation objectives; GT-Prior definition; conclusions and limitations
